1.explanation:
• docs/crossrefs/options.qmd shows the documented front-matter keys for crossref (including how to turn it on or off) — so we can confirm whether crossref:false is supported semantically.
• docs/crossrefs/simple.qmd and docs/crossrefs/all.qmd provide minimal and comprehensive cross-reference examples; they let us compare expected behavior when crossrefs are enabled.
• docs/crossrefs/unresolved.qmd shows how unresolved or suppressed crossrefs render, useful to see whether crossref:false should yield similar output.
• integration/formats/html contains HTML-format integration tests — we need to add or update tests here so that crossref:false under html is honored.
• smoke/crossref holds existing smoke tests for crossref behavior across formats; updating or adding a smoke test here will ensure the regression doesn’t recur and that crossref:false is fully supported.
1.bug_scenario:
In the user’s example, setting “crossref: false” under the html format block in YAML front matter isn’t recognized. The screenshot shows:

---
format:
  html:
    crossref: false  ⟵ underlined as invalid
filters:
  - testcrossref.lua
---

As a result, the editor flags the “false” value as an error and the build still generates cross-references. The user expects that specifying crossref: false under the html format would disable all cross-reference numbering in the HTML output, but this configuration key is not currently handled in the HTML format implementation or the crossref tests.
